question: Which of the following is a monosaccharide?

solution.why_correct: Glucose is a simple sugar (monosaccharide) -- the basic building block that cannot be broken down into simpler sugar units by hydrolysis.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sucrose is a disaccharide (glucose + fructose). Starch and cellulose are both polysaccharides, made of many repeating glucose units linked together -- none of these are single simple sugar units like glucose.
solution.concept_recap: Carbohydrate classification: monosaccharides (glucose, fructose -- simplest sugars), disaccharides (sucrose, lactose -- two monosaccharides linked), polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen -- many monosaccharides linked).

question: Statement I: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. Statement II: All 20 amino acids found in proteins have identical side chains (R groups).
options: Statement I is true; Statement II is false
Statement I is false; Statement II is true

solution.why_correct: Proteins are indeed polymers formed by amino acids joined via peptide bonds (Statement I true). However, Statement II is false -- each of the 20 standard amino acids has a UNIQUE side chain (R group), which is precisely what gives them different chemical properties and allows proteins to fold into diverse functional structures.
solution.why_others_wrong: B, C, D incorrectly accept that amino acids share identical side chains, but variation in the R group is the defining feature that distinguishes one amino acid from another and enables the vast diversity of protein structure/function.
solution.concept_recap: Amino acid structure: central carbon bonded to an amino group, carboxyl group, hydrogen, and a variable R group (side chain) that differs among all 20 standard amino acids, determining each one's unique chemical properties.
